sourceInformation.genre: A 3D sports and wellness anthology of balance activities round a small walkable island, with a daily-ritual meta game and a comedy story
sourceInformation.perspective: Third person: a chase camera on the island and a purpose-built camera for each activity
sourceInformation.tech: my-3dge at 2dbd829 (full workspace, engine read-only), three.js r182 on WebGPU, Rapier 0.21, Vite 7, TypeScript 5.9; HTML/CSS UI
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's native toon puppets and generators with new retreat assets: a clean, high-key brochure island
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's clip layer and humanoid with a new readable clip set scrubbed from the sim, so your thumb is the exercise
sourceInformation.audio: Tracker songs, defineSfx effects, Animalese-style gibberish syllable voices, all code, no audio files, music at 10% by default
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, ghost mode, up to 4; same-screen Group Class on its own, up to 4 pads
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripts allowed: bots on 10 seeds per activity, a scripted playthrough of the whole game, browser checks in Playwright, sparing screenshots; no review subagents
sourceInformation.research: The AI Hub protocol README and the my-3dge guide; nothing else was needed beyond the plan

testingFeedback: About 57 across the run, from wrong ids and lint to play-breaking bugs.

Ten: every same-screen player but the first having no balance disc, every class pose silently not playing (seats held no actor), a crash at the session scene start, a boot far past the hub deadline, the Programme restarting the first activity for ever, Gerald walking off the map after Island Jog, a press opening and closing the same screen, a frame crash in Pose Class, a crash removing the diving judges in mid-step, and the Carry on press dropping you straight back into the activity.

The scripted playthrough of the whole game with the human-like bot, which proved no softlock on three seeds and found the mid-step crash, and the page drive to the credits with one kind of input, which found the Programme loop and the Carry on bug that the sim could not see. Late on, a search for things written and never used found what every passing test had missed.
The look metrics from the shot tool: it told me the pale sky was blown out, and never that a dark band sat on the horizon. A screenshot found that in a second.
engineFeedback: Play is reproducible and needs no screen. Every activity could be played by bots on ten seeds at step speed, and replays matched in Node and Chromium first time. A pose as one line of numbers, scrubbed from the sim, was a joy.

Yes. Spawns inside setup are queued, so looking people up there silently gave every seat no body. I guessed wrong on the prop placement shape, on what describe returns, and on three library ids. The horizon took an hour.

The Wobble Model and the activity framework that makes eleven activities and a finale one shape, with bots; then the whole 10-foot front end: panels, Balance Disc, glyphs, Dev Mode, attract and the hub card.

Warm-up: the engine builds every registered prop's pipelines when the first prop arrives, which on a software GPU is past the hub's deadline, so a session scene has to draw its pavilion with no props at all.
Warm only the props a scene can spawn.
promptFeedback: The plan marks what was tested and gives real numbers, such as the sway rate that makes a thumb better than doing nothing. Its bots for judging feel were the right answer to nobody being able to play.
The plan was tested on an older engine commit and client hash than I got, so some of its details had moved. Its rule of two short sentences a line sits beside seed lines of five.
Judging feel and looks with no person and no real GPU: every sound by numbers, every picture on a software renderer at a few frames a second, and a 45-minute game to hold in one head.
Pin the engine commit and client version the plan was tested on, and give a boot-time budget for the island as well as the session, since warm-up cost drives how props should be made from the start.

aiHub.name: Teeter Fit
aiHub.tagline: Stand still. It is harder than it looks.
aiHub.description: A deadpan wellness retreat on an island balanced on one rock. Eleven balance activities, one verb, a Wobble Age, and a storm where your thumb holds the island level.
aiHub.controls: Lean: left stick, WASD or mouse · Feet: L2 R2, Q E or mouse buttons · Breathe: both
